title: R-FCN: Object Detection via Region-based Fully Convolutional Networks

problem.summary: Region-based detectors split into a shared convolutional subnetwork and an unshared RoI-wise subnetwork, so a deep per-region classifier is evaluated hundreds of times; naively making the whole network fully convolutional (RoI pooling after conv5) loses accuracy because classification wants translation invariance while detection needs translation variance.
statements: Per-RoI subnetworks repeat expensive computation for every region, hurting training and testing efficiency.
A fully convolutional detector with RoI pooling only after the last conv layer has considerably inferior accuracy.
Deepening the RoI-wise subnetwork (as in the ResNet detection pipeline) restores accuracy but reintroduces unshared per-region cost.

evidence.quote: However, as empirically investigated in this work, this naïve solution turns out to have considerably inferior detection accuracy that does not match the network’s superior classification accuracy.
We argue that the aforementioned unnatural design is caused by a dilemma of increasing translation invariance for image classification vs. respecting translation variance for object detection.
However, this design sacrifices training and testing efficiency since it introduces a considerable number of region-wise layers (Table 1).

background.summary: R-FCN follows the R-CNN/Fast/Faster R-CNN two-stage lineage, sharing computation with a semi-convolutional design, and converts fully convolutional classification backbones (ResNets) into detectors while borrowing position-sensitive ideas from instance-level FCNs.

relatedWork.name: R-CNN
relatedWork.relation: pioneered region proposals with deep networks but crops/warps each region without shared computation
relatedWork.quote: R-CNN [7] has demonstrated the effectiveness of using region proposals [27, 28] with deep networks.

relatedWork.name: SPPnet / Fast R-CNN / Faster R-CNN
relatedWork.relation: semi-convolutional predecessors: shared conv subnetwork plus per-region subnetwork
relatedWork.quote: SPPnet [8], Fast R-CNN [6], and Faster R-CNN [18] are “semiconvolutional”, in which a convolutional subnetwork performs shared computation on the entire image and another subnetwork evaluates individual regions.

relatedWork.name: Faster R-CNN (ResNet pipeline)
relatedWork.relation: inserts RoI pooling between conv4 and conv5, deepening the RoI-wise subnetwork at a speed cost
relatedWork.quote: To remedy this issue, in the ResNet paper [9] the RoI pooling layer of the Faster R-CNN detector [18] is unnaturally inserted between two sets of convolutional layers

relatedWork.name: RPN
relatedWork.relation: fully convolutional proposal generator whose features are shared with R-FCN
relatedWork.quote: The RPN component in Faster R-CNN [18] is a fully convolutional detector that predicts bounding boxes with respect to reference boxes (anchors) of multiple sizes.

relatedWork.name: Instance-sensitive FCN
relatedWork.relation: prior work that inspired position-sensitive score maps
relatedWork.quote: The concept of position-sensitive score maps is partially inspired by [3] that develops FCNs for instance-level semantic segmentation.

evidence.quote: We hypothesize that deeper convolutional layers in an image classification network are less sensitive to translation.
All learnable layers are convolutional and shared on the entire image, yet encode spatial information required for object detection.

solution.summary: R-FCN is a region-based detector in which every learnable layer is convolutional and computed on the whole image: the last conv layer emits k*k position-sensitive score maps per class, and a position-sensitive RoI pooling layer selectively pools each RoI bin from one map and votes, with no learnable layers after RoI pooling.
solution.approach: Position-sensitive score maps plus position-sensitive RoI pooling encode relative position so a fully convolutional network can both classify and localize regions.
components: ResNet-101 backbone using only convolutional layers (ImageNet pre-trained)
1x1 1024-d convolution for dimension reduction before the score-map layer
k*k position-sensitive score maps (k=7) with k*k*(C+1) channels
sibling 4k*k-d box regression bank with class-agnostic regression
position-sensitive RoI pooling with average voting and softmax scoring
RPN proposals with shared features via 4-step alternating training
à trous trick reducing effective stride from 32 to 16
online hard example mining at negligible per-RoI cost
non-maximum suppression at 0.3 IoU on 300 test RoIs

evidence.quote: To incorporate translation variance into FCN, we construct a set of position-sensitive score maps by using a bank of specialized convolutional layers as the FCN output.
R-FCN ends with a position-sensitive RoI pooling layer. This layer aggregates the outputs of the last convolutional layer and generates scores for each RoI.
Unlike [8, 6], our position-sensitive RoI layer conducts selective pooling, and each of the k × k bin aggregates responses from only one score map out of the bank of k × k score maps.
There is no learnable layer after the RoI layer, enabling nearly cost-free region-wise computation and speeding up both training and inference.

experiments.summary: R-FCN is compared with Faster R-CNN and alternative fully convolutional strategies on PASCAL VOC 2007/2012 and MS COCO using ResNet backbones, with ablations on position-sensitivity, stride/à trous, depth, proposal type, OHEM and multi-scale training, plus timing on a K40 GPU.

benchmarks.split: test-dev, trainval, multi-scale train and test
test-dev, trainval, multi-scale train and test

evidence.quote: We show competitive results on the PASCAL VOC datasets (e.g., 83.6% mAP on the 2007 set) with the 101-layer ResNet.
Its mAP (76.6%) is on par with the standard Faster R-CNN’s (76.4%, Table 3).
The à trous trick improves mAP by 2.6 points.

We note that our competitive result is obtained at a test speed of 0.17 seconds per image, 20× faster than Faster R-CNN +++ that takes 3.36 seconds as it further incorporates iterative box regression, context, and multi-scale testing [9].

limitations.summary: Gains saturate beyond ResNet-101 depth, position-sensitivity is mandatory (k=1 fails to converge), COCO results still trail Faster R-CNN +++, and mining more proposals gives no benefit.
items: Accuracy saturates: ResNet-152 gives no gain over ResNet-101.
The method depends on a k*k position-sensitive grid; with k=1 training does not converge.
On MS COCO the multi-scale model (31.5 AP) trails Faster R-CNN +++ (34.9 AP).
Mining from 2000 proposals adds cost with no benefit, so proposals are limited to 300.
Box regression is class-agnostic by default (class-specific variant only described as applicable).

evidence.quote: Our detection accuracy increases when the depth is increased from 50 to 101, but gets saturated with a depth of 152.
The importance of position-sensitivity is further demonstrated by setting k = 1, for which R-FCN is unable to converge.
This result is close to the 1st-place result (Faster R-CNN +++ with ResNet-101, 55.7%/34.9%) in the MS COCO 2015 competition.
But experiments show that mining from a larger set of candidates (e.g., 2000) has no benefit (Table 3).

futureDirections.direction: Adopt orthogonal FCN extensions developed for semantic segmentation and further region-based detection extensions, which the simple R-FCN system should absorb without difficulty.
futureDirections.quote: There have been a series of orthogonal extensions of FCNs that were developed for semantic segmentation (e.g., see [2]), as well as extensions of region-based methods for object detection (e.g., see [9, 1, 22]).

equations.name: multi-task loss
equations.expr: L(s, tx,y,w,h) = Lcls(sc*) + λ[c*>0] Lreg(t, t*)

deploymentClaims: 0.17 s per image test time on a K40 GPU (0.11 s on a Titan X), 2.5x faster than Faster R-CNN.

evidence.quote: With 300 RoIs at test time, Faster R-CNN takes 0.42s per image, 2.5× slower than our R-FCN that takes 0.17s per image (on a K40 GPU; this number is 0.11s on a Titan X GPU).
Code is made publicly available at: https://github.com/daijifeng001/r-fcn.
